packageRules.description: A major is a changelog to read, not a number to bump.
Actions are not automerged: checkout and setup-go build the environment make check evaluates in, so a bumped action is part of the gate rather than something the gate judges.
One pull request for the Go module set. Not automerged: make check runs go test, which links and executes the bumped module, so the code being judged produces the green check.
The Makefile's tool pins, grouped and not automerged: make check runs these tools to decide whether the bump that changed them is safe, so an automerged bump would validate itself.
go.mod's go directive is the minimum Go version for everyone importing this library. Raising it is a release decision, not a dependency bump; the workflows track the latest 1.27.x patch on their own.

customManagers.description: The Makefile's *_VERSION pins. Every tool is fetched with `go run pkg@version`, so the version lives beside the command that uses it rather than in go.mod.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix gets its pull request immediately rather than on Monday, but still waits for a human: vulnerabilityAlerts drops minimumReleaseAge, so automerging here would merge at zero age.
